mainTopic: הלל on the fourth cup: ברכת השיר, הלל הגדול and God feeding the world, and why the regular הלל is said
overview: The משנה says that on the fourth cup of the Seder we finish הלל and say ברכת השיר. The גמרא first asks what ברכת השיר is (רב יהודה: יהללוך; רבי יוחנן: נשמת). It then brings רבי טרפון's view that we also say הלל הגדול, gives three views on where הלל הגדול begins, and explains that it is 'great' because God feeds every creature. That theme leads to a series of teachings on how hard it is to provide food: harder than childbirth and than גאולה, and as hard as קריעת ים סוף. Teachings of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה follow, grouped by their author, about the body, the festivals, and לשון הרע. Then the גמרא asks why we also say the regular הלל, and answers that it contains five great themes, from יציאת מצרים to חבלו של משיח. Other answers point to the rescue of צדיקים from גיהנם and to חנניה, מישאל and עזריה in the fiery furnace. This leads to stories about גבריאל and אברהם in נמרוד's furnace and about the angel of hail, and גבריאל's plan to cool the furnace from within continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What is the blessing of song?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by ברכת השיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'blessing of song'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the משנה's term ברכת השיר means. It is setting up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says to finish הלל on the fourth cup and then say ברכת השיר, but it never says which text that is. The גמרא wants to identify the exact prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing of song, said at the end of הלל on the fourth cup
The fourth cup of the Seder

phrases.english: What is the 'blessing of song'?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה, which says that on the fourth cup you finish הלל and say ברכת השיר.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which text is the ברכת השיר mentioned in the משנה?

steps.title: רב יהודה: It is 'They shall praise You'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says ברכת השיר is יהללוך, the blessing that closes הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: It is 'They shall praise You, Lord our God.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives the first answer. ברכת השיר is the blessing יהללוך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהללוך is the closing blessing normally said right after הלל. In רב יהודה's view, the 'blessing of song' simply means the blessing that seals the song of הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They shall praise You', the closing blessing after הלל

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
'They shall praise You, Lord our God.'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: It is 'The breath of all living'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says ברכת השיר is נשמת כל חי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: It is 'The breath of all living.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different answer. ברכת השיר is נשמת כל חי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נשמת is the long praise we also say on שבת morning after פסוקי דזמרה. רבי יוחנן understands the 'song' to include this broader praise of God.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The breath of all living', a long prayer of praise
The verses of praise said in the morning prayers

steps.confusionAlert: Our הגדה includes both יהללוך and נשמת. Do not assume from that practice that the two opinions here agree. In the גמרא, each sage is giving his own answer to the question.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
'The breath of all living.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ברכת השיר is נשמת כל חי.

steps.title: רבי טרפון: Add הלל הגדול on the fourth cup
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי טרפון: on the fourth cup, finish הלל and also say הלל הגדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: On the fourth cup, one completes הלל over it and says הלל הגדול. These are the words of רבי טרפון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. In it, רבי טרפון says that on the fourth cup we add a second praise, הלל הגדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only mentioned finishing הלל and ברכת השיר. The ברייתא adds something new: רבי טרפון requires הלל הגדול as well. This leads directly into the next questions about what הלל הגדול is.

keyTerms.meaning: הלל הגדול, a special psalm of praise

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
On the fourth [cup], one completes the Hallel over it,
and says the Great Hallel,
these are the words of Rabbi Tarfon.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי טרפון, on the fourth cup one completes הלל and adds הלל הגדול.

steps.title: Others say: 'The Lord is my shepherd'
steps.stepSummary: Another opinion says to recite ה׳ רועי לא אחסר instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: 'The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second opinion. Instead of הלל הגדול, one says the psalm ה׳ רועי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ רועי (תהלים כ״ג) thanks God for providing food and care. That fits the end of a meal. It is offered as an alternative to רבי טרפון's הלל הגדול.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want' (תהלים כ״ג)

phrases.english: And some say:
'The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי טרפון about what to add on the fourth cup.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this view, one says ה׳ רועי rather than הלל הגדול.

steps.title: Where does הלל הגדול begin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which verses make up הלל הגדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where is הלל הגדול?
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבי טרפון mentioned הלל הגדול, the גמרא now asks where it starts. This sets up three answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that it ends before נהרות בבל (תהלים קל״ז). The only question is the starting point.

phrases.english: From where is the Great Hallel?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The starting and ending points of הלל הגדול.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: Only Psalm 136
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says it runs from הודו until נהרות בבל, meaning only תהלים קל״ו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: From 'Give thanks' until 'By the rivers of Babylon.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives the narrowest answer. הלל הגדול is just the psalm that starts with הודו (תהלים קל״ו).
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Until נהרות בבל' means up to that psalm, but not including it. So in this view, הלל הגדול is exactly one psalm, the one where every verse ends כי לעולם חסדו.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Give thanks', the opening of תהלים קל״ו
'The rivers of Babylon', the opening of תהלים קל״ז (the end point)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Until נהרות בבל' does NOT mean that נהרות בבל is included. It marks the point where הלל הגדול stops.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
From 'Give thanks' until 'The rivers of Babylon.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הלל הגדול is תהלים קל״ו alone.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Start from 'A song of ascents'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says it starts earlier, at שיר המעלות (תהלים קל״ד).
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן says: From 'A song of ascents' until 'By the rivers of Babylon.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the widest answer. He starts two psalms earlier, at the last שיר המעלות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view, הלל הגדול covers תהלים קל״ד, קל״ה and קל״ו. All of them speak of praising God and His kindness.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A song of ascents', here meaning תהלים קל״ד

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan says:
From 'A song of ascents' until 'The rivers of Babylon.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הלל הגדול is תהלים קל״ד through קל״ו.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: Start from 'For God chose Jacob'
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב starts in the middle of תהלים קל״ה, at כי יעקב בחר לו יה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: From 'For God chose Jacob for Himself' until 'By the rivers of Babylon.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב gives a middle answer. He starts at verse 4 of תהלים קל״ה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His starting point lies between the other two opinions. It begins where the psalm starts describing God choosing Israel and His great acts for them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For God chose Jacob for Himself' (תהלים קל״ה:ד)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on where הלל הגדול starts: קל״ו (רבי יהודה), קל״ה:ד (רב אחא בר יעקב), and קל״ד (רבי יוחנן). All agree that it ends before נהרות בבל.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
From 'For God chose Jacob for Himself'
until 'The rivers of Babylon.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הלל הגדול is תהלים קל״ה:ד through קל״ו.

steps.title: Why is it called הלל הגדול?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes this הלל 'great'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is it called הלל הגדול?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the name הלל הגדול. It is setting up רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already have a regular הלל (תהלים קי״ג to קי״ח). So the גמרא wants to know what special theme makes this one 'great'.

keyTerms.meaning: And why is it called by this name?

phrases.english: And why is it called the Great Hallel?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the title הלל הגדול.

steps.title: Because God sits on high and feeds every creature
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that it praises the הקדוש ברוך הוא for feeding every creature from His high place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Because the Holy One, Blessed be He, sits in the heights of the world and gives out food to every creature.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers that it is 'great' because it describes God, from on high, giving food to every creature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The psalm includes the verse נותן לחם לכל בשר ('Who gives bread to all flesh'). God is exalted and yet personally sustains every living thing, and that makes this praise especially great.
steps.whyThisMatters: This fits the Seder well. Right after eating a meal, we praise God as the One who feeds everyone.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Because the Holy One, Blessed be He,
sits in the heights of the world
and gives out food to every creature.
phrases.notes: Based on תהלים קל״ו:כ״ה, 'Who gives bread to all flesh.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is called great because it praises God's providing food for all creatures from His exalted place.

steps.title: The 26 times הודו appears match 26 generations before מתן תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says the 26 verses of הודו match the 26 generations before מתן תורה, whom God fed out of pure kindness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: These twenty-six 'Give thanks', what do they correspond to? They correspond to the twenty-six generations that the Holy One, Blessed be He, created in His world and did not give the Torah to, yet He fed them through His kindness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי adds a new idea about the psalm. Its 26 verses, each ending כי לעולם חסדו, stand for 26 generations that lived before the Torah was given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were 10 generations from אדם to נח, 10 from נח to אברהם, and 6 more (יצחק, יעקב, לוי, קהת, עמרם, משה) until מתן תורה. These generations had no Torah to earn merit, so God kept them alive purely out of חסד. That is why each verse repeats כי לעולם חסדו.

keyTerms.meaning: Through His kindness (not because they deserved it)

steps.whatToRemember: הלל הגדול is about God's kindness in feeding the world. Its 26 verses recall the 26 generations who survived only through His חסד, before there was any Torah.
steps.whyThisMatters: This connects the name 'great' to the repeated refrain כי לעולם חסדו. The praise is for kindness given without any merit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
These twenty-six 'Give thanks',
what do they correspond to?
To the twenty-six generations
that the Holy One, Blessed be He, created in His world
and did not give them the Torah,
and He fed them through His kindness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי יוחנן's theme of God feeding all creatures, and explains why the psalm has 26 verses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 26 verses of הודו correspond to the 26 pre-Torah generations, who were sustained only by God's חסד.

steps.title: Thanking God for punishing each person according to what they can handle
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that הודו לה׳ כי טוב means we thank ה׳ for collecting a person's 'debt' (punishment for sin) from his own possessions, scaled to what he has.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: What does the פסוק 'Give thanks to ה׳ for He is good' mean? Give thanks to ה׳ who collects a person's debt through his own good things: a rich man through his ox, a poor man through his sheep, an orphan through his egg, a widow through her chicken.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a new reading of the פסוק הודו לה׳ כי טוב, the opening of the הלל הגדול just discussed. He says the 'good' of ה׳ is that He punishes each person only with what that person can afford to lose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He plays on the word טוב: ה׳ collects a person's חוב (debt of sin) בטובתו, from his own goods. A rich man loses an ox, but a widow only loses a chicken, so nobody is crushed beyond his means. This fits the theme of ה׳ caring for each creature in a fitting way.

keyTerms.meaning: His debt; here, the punishment owed for his sins
Through his good things (his own property)

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
What is the meaning of what is written: 'Give thanks to ה׳ for He is good'?
phrases.notes: תהלים קל״ו:א, the start of the הלל הגדול.

phrases.aramaic: הוֹדוּ לַה׳ שֶׁגּוֹבֶה חוֹבָתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם בְּטוֹבָתוֹ:
phrases.english: Give thanks to ה׳, who collects a person's debt through his own good things:
phrases.notes: There's a play on words here: טוב (good) and טובתו (his goods).

phrases.english: a rich man through his ox, and a poor man through his sheep,
an orphan through his egg, a widow through her chicken.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״הוֹדוּ לַה׳ כִּי טוֹב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the פסוקים of the הלל הגדול, now focusing on the opening words הודו לה׳ כי טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ is 'good' because He collects a person's punishment from his own possessions, in proportion to what he has, never more than he can bear.

steps.title: Earning a living is twice as hard as giving birth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן proves from a word difference in the פסוקים that earning food is twice as hard as childbirth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: A person's food is twice as hard as a woman giving birth. For about childbirth it says 'בעצב' (in pain), but about food it says 'בעצבון' (in great toil).
steps.whatsHappening: Building on the theme of ה׳ feeding the world, רבי יוחנן shows how hard it is to get food. He compares it to childbirth, using the curses given after the חטא of עץ הדעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both curses use the same root עצב (pain), but the woman's curse says בעצב while the man's curse says בעצבון, a longer, stronger form. רבי יוחנן reads the extra letters as 'double' the pain. This shows why ה׳ deserves special praise for providing food.

keyTerms.meaning: In pain (said to חוה about childbirth)
In great toil (said to אדם about food)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
A person's food is difficult
twice as much as a woman giving birth,
for about a woman giving birth it is written: 'In pain',
while about food it is written: 'In toil'.
phrases.notes: בראשית ג:יז; the longer word means greater pain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: קָשִׁין מְזוֹנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם כִּפְלַיִים כַּיּוֹלֵדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new statement about how hard it is to get food, supporting why ה׳ is praised for feeding everyone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Earning a living is twice as hard as childbirth, learned from בעצבון versus בעצב.

steps.title: Earning a living is harder than redemption
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן proves from יעקב's words that food is harder than גאולה: an angel can redeem, but only ה׳ Himself provides food.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: A person's food is harder than redemption. About redemption it says 'The angel who redeemed me from all evil', just a regular angel. But about food it says 'The God who shepherds me'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second comparison showing how hard פרנסה is. He uses יעקב's ברכה to his grandsons, where two different 'helpers' are mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the same ברכה, יעקב credits a מלאך with saving him from harm, but credits אלקים Himself with feeding him. Since saving can be handed to an angel but feeding needs ה׳ directly, feeding must be the harder task.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who shepherds (feeds and cares for)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: קָשִׁין מְזוֹנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם יוֹתֵר מִן הַגְּאוּלָּה,
phrases.english: A person's food is more difficult than redemption,
for about redemption it is written:
'The angel who redeemed me from all evil',
merely an angel,
whereas about food it is written: 'The God who shepherds me'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: קָשִׁין מְזוֹנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם יוֹתֵר מִן הַגְּאוּלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second statement of the same רבי יוחנן on the same theme, now comparing food to גאולה instead of childbirth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Earning a living is harder than גאולה, since an angel redeems but ה׳ Himself feeds.

steps.title: אדם cries over eating like an animal and is comforted by bread
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי tells that אדם הראשון wept when told the land would grow thorns for him, fearing he would eat like his donkey, and calmed down when told he would eat bread by his sweat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: When the הקדוש ברוך הוא told אדם 'Thorns and thistles it will grow for you', his eyes ran with tears. He said: Master of the world, will my donkey and I eat from one trough? Once ה׳ told him 'By the sweat of your brow you will eat bread', his mind was calmed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story about the curse of earning food, continuing the same theme. אדם fears he will be lowered to an animal's level, and ה׳'s next words reassure him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Thorns and thistles' and 'grass of the field' sounded like animal food, so אדם cried. The next פסוק says he will eat bread, which takes human work (plowing, baking), so a person stays above animals even in hard labor. The toil itself is what keeps him human.

keyTerms.meaning: By the sweat of your face

steps.whatToRemember: This whole section praises ה׳ as the One who feeds every creature. Earning food is very hard (harder than childbirth and גאולה), yet ה׳ provides it in a way that keeps people human and never punishes beyond what they can bear.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לָאָדָם
phrases.english: When the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Adam
'Thorns and thistles it will grow for you'
phrases.notes: בראשית ג:יח, which continues 'and you will eat the grass of the field'.

phrases.english: his eyes streamed with tears,
He said before Him: Master of the World,
will my donkey and I eat from one trough?

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ: ״בְּזֵעַת אַפֶּךָ תֹּאכַל לֶחֶם״,
phrases.english: Once He said to him: 'By the sweat of your brow you will eat bread',
his mind was calmed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לָאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the hardship of earning food, using the same curse to אדם that רבי יוחנן quoted in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אדם was comforted that, though he must work hard, he would eat human bread and not animal food.

steps.title: We would have been better off eating grass
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says we would have been lucky if the first curse, eating the plants of the field, had stayed in place. He adds that we still have not fully escaped it, because we still eat field greens.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: We would have been fortunate if we had stayed under the first decree. And we still have not fully escaped it, because we still eat the grass of the field.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש reacts to the story in step 16. There, אדם הראשון was relieved to be told he would eat bread by his sweat instead of grass like an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אדם was happy to trade grass for bread. ריש לקיש says the trade cost us a lot, because bread takes enormous work to produce, while field plants simply grow. He also notes that part of the first decree is still with us, since we still eat vegetables and leaves.

keyTerms.meaning: Under the first decree (eating field plants)
Grass or herbs of the field

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not arguing with the story in step 16. He is giving his own view on which outcome was really better for us.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Fortunate would we be had we remained under the first decree,
phrases.notes: The first decree means eating the plants of the field, without the hard labor of making bread.

phrases.english: and we still have not escaped from it,
since we eat the grass of the field.
phrases.notes: This refers to vegetables and leafy greens.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the story of אדם הראשון in step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Staying with the first decree (field plants) would have been better, and part of it still remains with us.

steps.title: Providing food is as hard as splitting the sea
steps.stepSummary: רב שיזבי, quoting רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, says that providing a person's food is as difficult as קריעת ים סוף. He learns this from two פסוקים in הלל הגדול that are read together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי said in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: A person's food is as difficult as the splitting of the Red Sea. It is written, "He gives bread to all flesh," and next to it, "To Him who split the Red Sea into parts."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another teaching that shows how hard it is to provide food. This time food is compared to the splitting of the sea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים appear in the same psalm, תהלים קל״ו, and both end with the same refrain, כי לעולם חסדו. The גמרא treats them as linked, so feeding the world counts as a miracle on the level of קריעת ים סוף.

keyTerms.meaning: The splitting of the Red Sea
And placed next to it (a link between two פסוקים)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁיזְבִי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה:
phrases.english: Rav Sheizvi said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya:
A person's food is as difficult
as the splitting of the Red Sea,
as it is written: "He gives bread to all flesh,"
and linked to it: "To Him who split the Red Sea into parts."
phrases.notes: תהלים קל״ו:י״ג. This is in the same psalm, with the same refrain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁיזְבִי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more comparison to the series on how hard food is to provide
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Providing food is as difficult as קריעת ים סוף.

steps.title: Relieving oneself is like being saved from death
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says that when a person cannot relieve himself, opening his body is as hard as being saved from death and as hard as קריעת ים סוף. He learns this from two neighboring פסוקים in ישעיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said: A person's openings are as difficult as the day of death and as the splitting of the Red Sea. As it says, "The one who is bent over will quickly be opened," and after it, "Who stirs up the sea and its waves roar."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from רבי אלעזר בן עזריה with the same style, comparing a daily bodily need to death and to the splitting of the sea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק describes a person bent over being opened up. It continues that he will not die into the pit, which shows the danger is like death. The very next פסוק speaks of stirring up the sea, which links the opening to קריעת ים סוף.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is bent over or confined

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said:
A person's orifices are as difficult
phrases.notes: This means when he cannot relieve himself properly.

phrases.english: as the day of death and as the splitting of the Red Sea,
as it is stated: "The one who is bent over will speedily be opened,"
phrases.notes: ישעיה נ״א:י״ד. The פסוק continues, "and he shall not die into the pit," which supplies the death comparison.

phrases.english: and after it is written: "Who stirs up the sea and its waves roar."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה: קָשִׁין נְקָבָיו שֶׁל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same חכם and same method of reading neighboring פסוקים, applied to a new subject
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A blocked body being opened is as great a rescue as being saved from death and as קריעת ים סוף.

steps.title: Disrespecting the festivals is like idol worship
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת, quoting רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, says that anyone who treats the מועדים with contempt is like someone who serves עבודה זרה. He learns this because the איסור of molten idols is placed right before the מצוה to keep פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת said in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: Anyone who disrespects the festivals is as if he worships idols. As it says, "Do not make molten gods for yourself," and right after it, "Keep the Festival of מצות."
steps.whatsHappening: Having quoted רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, the גמרא adds one more of his teachings. This one has nothing to do with food; it appears here only because it comes from the same חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method is again two פסוקים placed next to each other, in שמות ל״ד. Because the warning against idols comes right before the command to keep חג המצות, disrespecting the festival is treated as close to עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who treats with contempt or disrespect

steps.whatToRemember: The teachings of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה in this series all use the same tool: two פסוקים placed next to each other are read as comparing their subjects. This teaching, and the one after it, are grouped here by their author, not by their topic.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not try to connect this teaching to the food theme. It appears here only because it is another saying of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how seriously חז״ל viewed respect for the יום טוב, which fits a מסכת about פסח.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה:
phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya:
Anyone who disparages the festivals
is as if he worships idols,
as it is stated: "You shall not make molten gods for yourself,"
and after it is written: "The Festival of Matzot you shall keep."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grouped with the previous steps by author (רבי אלעזר בן עזריה), not by topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Disrespecting the מועדים is compared to serving עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Speakers, accepters, and false witnesses deserve to be thrown to the dogs
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת, quoting רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, says that whoever speaks לשון הרע, accepts לשון הרע, or gives false testimony deserves to be thrown to the dogs. He learns this from two neighboring פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת also said in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: Anyone who speaks slander, anyone who accepts slander, and anyone who testifies falsely against his friend deserves to be thrown to the dogs. The verse says, 'You shall throw it to the dog,' and right after it is written, 'Do not accept a false report.' And you can also read it as 'Do not cause others to accept.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the next teaching in the same series by רב ששת in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. This time the subject is people who spread or believe lies about others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about throwing טריפה meat to the dogs comes right before the פסוק 'לא תשא שמע שוא'. Because the two are placed next to each other, the גמרא connects them: whoever is described in the second פסוק deserves the 'dogs' of the first. Reading תשא as 'accept' covers the listener. The extra reading תַּשִּׂיא, 'cause others to accept', covers the speaker. The rest of that פסוק talks about being a false witness, which covers the third person in the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Negative or damaging speech about another person
The one who accepts and believes what he hears
And read it as: a second way of reading the same letters
After it, right next to it

steps.whatToRemember: The speaker, the listener who believes it, and the false witness are all treated as equally serious. The source is two פסוקים placed next to each other, plus a second reading of the word תשא.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה:
phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya:
Anyone who speaks slander,
and anyone who accepts slander,
and anyone who testifies falsely against his friend,
deserves to be thrown to the dogs,
as it says: 'You shall throw it to the dog,'
and right after it is written: 'Do not accept a false report,'
and read it also as: 'Do not cause others to accept.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching in the same chain of sayings by רב ששת in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, again learned from neighboring פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Speaking לשון הרע, accepting it, and giving false testimony each make a person deserving of being thrown to the dogs.

steps.title: Why say the regular הלל if הלל הגדול exists?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: since we have הלל הגדול, which was praised earlier, why do we also say the regular הלל?
steps.simpleTranslation: And since there is הלל הגדול, what is the reason that we say this one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of הלל and asks a question. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא praised הלל הגדול because it mentions that ה׳ gives food to all creatures. If that הלל is so special, it seems we would not also need the regular הלל. The question asks what special content the regular הלל has.

keyTerms.meaning: הלל הגדול, תהלים קל״ו ('כי לעולם חסדו')

steps.confusionAlert: 'הַאי', 'this one', means the regular הלל we say on every יום טוב (תהלים קי״ג–קי״ח). It does not mean הלל הגדול.

phrases.english: And since there is the Great Hallel,
what is the reason that we say this one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the series of sayings by רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and returns to the discussion of הלל הגדול from steps 10-11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What special value does the regular הלל have that makes it worth saying when הלל הגדול exists?

steps.title: The regular הלל contains five great themes
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the regular הלל includes five major themes: יציאת מצרים, קריעת ים סוף, מתן תורה, תחיית המתים, and חבלו של משיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it contains these five things: the Exodus from Egypt, the splitting of the Sea, the giving of the Torah, the resurrection of the dead, and the birth pangs of the Messiah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The regular הלל is special because it covers five central events in Jewish history and in the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל הגדול is praised for one theme: ה׳ feeding all creatures. The regular הלל covers the whole story, from past redemption to future redemption. That gives it its own importance. The next steps will show where each theme appears.

keyTerms.meaning: The giving of the Torah at הר סיני
The 'birth pangs' of משיח: the suffering before the final redemption

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה דְבָרִים הַלָּלוּ:
phrases.english: Because it contains these five things:
the Exodus from Egypt, the splitting of the Sea,
and the giving of the Torah, and the resurrection of the dead,
and the birth pangs of the Messiah.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה דְבָרִים הַלָּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The regular הלל is said because it contains these five great themes together: יציאת מצרים, קריעת ים סוף, מתן תורה, תחיית המתים, and חבלו של משיח.

steps.title: Sources in הלל for the first four themes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows a פסוק in הלל for יציאת מצרים, קריעת ים סוף, מתן תורה, and תחיית המתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Exodus from Egypt, as it is written: 'When Israel went out of Egypt.' The splitting of the Sea, as it is written: 'The sea saw and fled.' The giving of the Torah, as it is written: 'The mountains danced like rams.' The resurrection of the dead, as it is written: 'I will walk before ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves its answer by pointing to a פסוק in הלל for each of the first four themes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two are stated openly in בצאת ישראל. 'The mountains danced' refers to הר סיני shaking at מתן תורה. 'I will walk before ה׳ in the lands of the living' comes right after 'You saved my soul from death'. So it is read as life after death, which is תחיית המתים.

phrases.english: The Exodus from Egypt, as it is written: 'When Israel went out of Egypt.'

phrases.aramaic: וּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף, דִּכְתִיב: ״הַיָּם רָאָה וַיָּנוֹס״.
phrases.english: And the splitting of the Sea, as it is written: 'The sea saw and fled.'
The giving of the Torah, as it is written: 'The mountains danced like rams.'
The resurrection of the dead, as it is written: 'I will walk before ה׳.'
phrases.notes: תהלים קט״ז:ט, 'in the lands of the living'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the list of five themes from step 23 with פסוקים.
steps.raayaObject: That the regular הלל contains the first four of the five themes
steps.raayaSupportSource: פסוקים from תהלים קי״ד and קט״ז

steps.title: The fifth theme: 'לא לנו' refers to שעבוד מלכיות
steps.stepSummary: The source for חבלו של משיח is 'לא לנו ה׳ לא לנו'. רבי יוחנן explains that this פסוק refers to the oppression of Israel by the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: The birth pangs of the Messiah, as it is written: 'Not for us, ה׳, not for us.' And רבי יוחנן said: 'Not for us, ה׳, not for us' refers to the enslavement under the kingdoms.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the פסוק for the fifth theme. It then brings רבי יוחנן to explain why this פסוק is about חבלו של משיח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its own, 'לא לנו' does not obviously speak about משיח. רבי יוחנן reads it as a prayer from the time when the nations rule over Israel and ask 'Where is their God?'. That painful period before the redemption is חבלו של משיח.

keyTerms.meaning: Not for us: opening words of תהלים קט״ו
Being oppressed and ruled by the nations

phrases.aramaic: חֶבְלוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ, דִּכְתִיב: ״לֹא לָנוּ ה׳ לֹא לָנוּ״,
phrases.english: The birth pangs of the Messiah, as it is written: 'Not for us, ה׳, not for us,'

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: ״לֹא לָנוּ ה׳ לֹא לָנוּ״ —
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan said: 'Not for us, ה׳, not for us'
this refers to the enslavement under the kingdoms.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֶבְלוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ, דִּכְתִיב: ״לֹא לָנוּ ה׳ לֹא לָנוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of sources by giving the fifth theme, with רבי יוחנן's explanation.
steps.raayaObject: That the regular הלל contains חבלו של משיח
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים קט״ו:א, as explained by רבי יוחנן

steps.title: Another version: 'לא לנו' refers to the war of גוג ומגוג
steps.stepSummary: Some report רבי יוחנן differently: 'לא לנו' refers to the war of גוג ומגוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רבי יוחנן said: 'Not for us, ה׳, not for us' refers to the war of Gog and Magog.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of what רבי יוחנן said about the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree that the פסוק speaks of the hard times before the redemption. They differ on which hardship it means. In the first version it is the long exile under the nations. In the second it is the final war of גוג ומגוג at the end of days. Either way, the regular הלל contains the theme of חבלו של משיח.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: introduces another version of a teaching
The great war of the nations against Israel at the end of days

steps.whatToRemember: The regular הלל is said because it covers five great themes: יציאת מצרים, קריעת ים סוף, מתן תורה, תחיית המתים, and חבלו של משיח. The last is found in 'לא לנו', read either as שעבוד מלכיות or as the war of גוג ומגוג.

phrases.english: Some say that Rabbi Yochanan said:
'Not for us, ה׳, not for us'
this refers to the war of Gog and Magog.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רבי יוחנן's statement from step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the second version, 'לא לנו' refers to the war of גוג ומגוג.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: הלל mentions saving souls from גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives another reason for saying the regular הלל: it speaks about saving the souls of צדיקים from גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Because it contains the rescue of the souls of the righteous from גיהנם, as it says: 'Please, ה׳, save my soul.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer to the question of step 22: why do we also say the regular הלל? רב נחמן בר יצחק points to a theme in it that was not on the earlier list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer listed five themes. רב נחמן בר יצחק adds that הלל also speaks about saving צדיקים from גיהנם. His proof is the פסוק 'אנה ה׳ מלטה נפשי', which he reads as a plea to be saved from גיהנם.

keyTerms.meaning: גיהנם, the place where souls are punished after death

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Because it contains
the rescue of the souls of the righteous from Gehinnom,
as it says: 'Please, ה׳, save my soul.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the question of step 22, after the themes listed in steps 23-26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why do we also say the regular הלל?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because it mentions the rescue of צדיקים from גיהנם.

steps.title: חזקיה: הלל describes the righteous going into the fiery furnace and coming out
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה says the regular הלל is special because it contains the story of צדיקים going down into the fiery furnace and coming back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: Because it contains the going down of the righteous into the fiery furnace, and their coming up out of it.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה gives yet another reason we say the regular הלל. He states his idea in general terms here, and the גמרא will explain it in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'righteous' here are חנניה, מישאל and עזריה, whom נבוכדנצר threw into a furnace (דניאל ג׳). חזקיה says both their going in and their coming out are hinted at in הלל.

phrases.english: Chizkiyah said:
Because it contains
the going down of the righteous into the fiery furnace,
and their coming up out of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer to the same question, alongside רב נחמן בר יצחק's.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why do we also say the regular הלל?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because it contains the going down of צדיקים into the furnace and their coming out.

steps.title: The going down into the furnace: who said each verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows where the going down into the furnace appears in הלל. Each of חנניה, מישאל and עזריה said one part of the פסוק, and the last part they said together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their going down, as it is written: 'Not to us, ה׳, not to us' — חנניה said; 'but to Your name give glory' — מישאל said; 'for Your kindness and for Your truth' — עזריה said; 'Why should the nations say' — they all said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the first half of חזקיה's claim. It divides the פסוקים of 'לא לנו' among the three צדיקים as they were about to go into the fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each piece fits someone about to give up their life: 'not for our honor, but for Your name.' The ending, 'why should the nations say, where is their God,' was said by all three together. It shows they were willing to die so that ה׳'s name would not be shamed.

keyTerms.meaning: the three צדיקים thrown into the furnace by נבוכדנצר

steps.confusionAlert: In step 25, רבי יוחנן used 'לא לנו' for חבלו של משיח. Here חזקיה reads the same פסוק as the words of חנניה, מישאל and עזריה. These are two different readings of one פסוק.

phrases.english: Their going down, as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא לָנוּ ה׳ לֹא לָנוּ״ אָמַר חֲנַנְיָה,
phrases.english: 'Not to us, ה׳, not to us' — Chananya said,
'but to Your name give glory' — Mishael said,
'for Your kindness and for Your truth' — Azarya said,
'Why should the nations say' — they all said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first half (the going down) of חזקיה's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That the going down into the furnace is in הלל
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים קט״ו:א׳-ב׳, 'לא לנו ה׳ לא לנו'

steps.title: Coming out of the furnace: who said each verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows where coming out of the furnace appears in הלל: the short chapter 'הללו את ה׳ כל גוים', split among the three and ending with everyone together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their coming up from the fiery furnace, as it is written: 'Praise ה׳, all nations' — חנניה said; 'laud Him, all peoples' — מישאל said; 'for His kindness overpowered us' — עזריה said; 'and the truth of ה׳ is forever, הללויה' — they all said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the second half of חזקיה's claim. When the three came out alive, they praised ה׳ with the פסוקים of 'הללו את ה׳ כל גוים'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The miracle happened in front of all the nations, so the praise calls on the nations to praise ה׳. As before, each one said a line, and all three said the final line together.

phrases.english: Their coming up from the fiery furnace, as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״הַלְלוּ אֶת ה׳ כׇּל גּוֹיִם״ אָמַר חֲנַנְיָה,
phrases.english: 'Praise ה׳, all nations' — Chananya said,
'laud Him, all peoples' — Mishael said,
'for His kindness overpowered us' — Azarya said,
'and the truth of ה׳ is forever, Halleluyah' — they all said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the second half (the coming out) of חזקיה's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That coming out of the furnace is in הלל
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים קי״ז, 'הללו את ה׳ כל גוים'

steps.title: Some say the angel גבריאל said the last verse
steps.stepSummary: A different opinion: the line 'ואמת ה׳ לעולם' was not said by the three together but by the angel גבריאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: 'And the truth of ה׳ is forever' — גבריאל said it.
steps.whatsHappening: A יש אומרים changes who said the last line. This line sets up the story that follows, which explains why גבריאל would say it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 30, all three said 'ואמת ה׳ לעולם'. Here it is given to גבריאל instead. We do not yet know why. The story of אברהם and נמרוד will explain it.

phrases.english: And some say:
'And the truth of ה׳ is forever' — Gavriel said it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 30 about who said the final line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ואמת ה׳ לעולם' was said by גבריאל.

steps.title: גבריאל offers to save אברהם from נמרוד's furnace
steps.stepSummary: The story begins: when נמרוד threw אברהם אבינו into a furnace, גבריאל asked הקב״ה for permission to go down, cool the fire, and save him.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the wicked נמרוד threw our father אברהם into the fiery furnace, גבריאל said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the World, I will go down and cool it, and save the righteous man from the fiery furnace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story to explain why גבריאל is linked to the line 'ואמת ה׳ לעולם'. This step sets up the scene: גבריאל offers to help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was an earlier furnace story, with אברהם, long before חנניה, מישאל and עזריה. גבריאל, the angel connected with fire, offers to cool it and save אברהם. The next step tells הקב״ה's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: the wicked נמרוד, the king who threw אברהם into the fire

phrases.english: When the wicked Nimrod threw

phrases.aramaic: אֶת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ לְתוֹךְ כִּבְשַׁן הָאֵשׁ
phrases.english: our father Avraham into the fiery furnace,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר גַּבְרִיאֵל לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Gavriel said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the World,
I will go down and cool it,
and save the righteous man from the fiery furnace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the background story behind the יש אומרים of step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גבריאל offered to save אברהם from נמרוד's furnace.

steps.title: ה׳ answers: the One and Only should save the one and only
steps.stepSummary: הקב״ה turns down גבריאל's offer. He is unique in His world and אברהם is unique in his, so it is fitting for the Unique One to save the unique one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him: I am unique in My world, and he is unique in his world; it is fitting for the unique one to save the unique one.
steps.whatsHappening: הקב״ה answers גבריאל and says He will save אברהם Himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At that time אברהם was the only one in the world who knew and served ה׳, just as ה׳ is One. Because of this special match, הקב״ה saved אברהם personally and not through an angel.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him:
I am unique in My world,
and he is unique in his world;
it is fitting for the unique one to save the unique one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: הקב״ה's reply to גבריאל's offer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקב״ה saved אברהם Himself, because the Unique One should save the unique one.

steps.title: גבריאל is rewarded: he will save three of אברהם's descendants
steps.stepSummary: Since הקב״ה never withholds reward for good intentions, He told גבריאל that he would save three of אברהם's descendants: חנניה, מישאל and עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not withhold the reward of any creature, He said: You will merit to save three of his descendants.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends by connecting back to the furnace of חנניה, מישאל and עזריה. That explains why גבריאל said 'ואמת ה׳ לעולם' when they came out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גבריאל only offered to help, yet הקב״ה rewarded even that wish. His reward was to rescue חנניה, מישאל and עזריה. That is why, according to the יש אומרים, he was the one who said 'ואמת ה׳ לעולם': ה׳ kept His promise to him.

keyTerms.meaning: does not withhold or cut short

steps.whatToRemember: The regular הלל holds many hidden stories. One is the furnace of חנניה, מישאל and עזריה, with each line said by one of them. According to the יש אומרים, the last line was said by גבריאל, who was rewarded for wanting to save אברהם.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that הקב״ה rewards even a good intention that never got carried out.

phrases.english: And since the Holy One, Blessed be He
does not withhold the reward of any creature,
He said: You will merit to save
three of his descendants.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְפִי שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֵינוֹ מְקַפֵּחַ שְׂכַר כׇּל בְּרִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story and ties it back to step 31.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: גבריאל saved חנניה, מישאל and עזריה as a reward, so he said 'ואמת ה׳ לעולם'.

steps.title: The hail angel offers to cool the furnace
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון השילוני teaches that when נבוכדנצר threw חנניה, מישאל and עזריה into the furnace, יורקמו, the angel of hail, asked הקב״ה for permission to go down, cool the furnace, and save them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון השילוני taught: When the wicked נבוכדנצר threw חנניה, מישאל and עזריה into the fiery furnace, יורקמו, the angel in charge of hail, stood before הקב״ה and said: Master of the world, I will go down, cool the furnace, and save these צדיקים from the fiery furnace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new scene in the furnace story, taught by רבי שמעון השילוני. An angel named יורקמו, who is in charge of hail, volunteers to rescue the three צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the previous steps, הקב״ה promised גבריאל that he would get to save three of אברהם's descendants. Now the moment arrives, but a different angel, the hail angel, steps forward first. This sets up a contest over who will actually do the rescue.

keyTerms.meaning: יורקמו, the angel in charge of hail
Master of the world (a way of addressing הקב״ה)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon HaShiloni taught:
When the wicked Nebuchadnezzar threw
Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah
into the fiery furnace,
Yurkamo, the angel of hail, stood up
phrases.notes: Each force of nature has an angel in charge of it.

phrases.english: before the Holy One, Blessed be He,
and said before Him: Master of the world,
I will go down and cool the furnace
and I will save these righteous men
from the fiery furnace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the story from the promise to גבריאל to the actual furnace of חנניה, מישאל and עזריה, where another angel volunteers first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The angel of hail offered to cool the furnace and rescue the three צדיקים.

steps.title: גבריאל rejects the hail angel's plan
steps.stepSummary: גבריאל argues that a hail angel putting out fire would not show הקב״ה's greatness, because everyone knows water puts out fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: גבריאל said to him: הקב״ה's power will not be shown this way, because you are the angel of hail, and everyone knows that water puts out fire.
steps.whatsHappening: גבריאל pushes back on יורקמו's offer. He says that rescue would look natural, not miraculous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal is not only to save the צדיקים but to show הקב״ה's power to the world. If hail cools a fire, people will say it was just nature, since water beats fire. So the hail angel's plan fails at the main purpose.
steps.confusionAlert: גבריאל is not saying the hail angel couldn't do it. He agrees it would work. His objection is that it would look ordinary and not show הקב״ה's greatness.

phrases.english: Gabriel said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין גְּבוּרָתוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּכָךְ
phrases.english: The power of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not shown in this way
since you are the angel of hail,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַכֹּל יוֹדְעִין שֶׁהַמַּיִם מְכַבִּין אֶת הָאֵשׁ.
phrases.english: and everyone knows that water puts out fire.
phrases.notes: So the rescue would look natural, not like a miracle.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ גַּבְרִיאֵל: אֵין גְּבוּרָתוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects the proposal made by יורקמו in step 35.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole plan of having the hail angel do the rescue.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Water putting out fire is natural, so the rescue would not display הקב״ה's power.

steps.title: גבריאל offers a greater miracle: fire cooling from within
steps.stepSummary: גבריאל proposes that he, the angel of fire, go down and cool the furnace from the inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, I am the angel of fire. I will go down and cool the furnace from the inside.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected יורקמו's plan, גבריאל offers his own. His sentence is not finished here; the גמרא continues it on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fire cooling itself from within is the opposite of nature, so it would clearly be a miracle that shows הקב״ה's power. This also fits step 34, where הקב״ה promised גבריאל that he would save these three descendants of אברהם.

keyTerms.meaning: The angel in charge of fire

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties back to the earlier promise. גבריאל, who was not allowed to save אברהם, is now the one who saves אברהם's descendants, and in the most miraculous way possible.

phrases.english: Rather, I, the angel of fire,
will go down and cool it from the inside,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אֲנִי שַׂר שֶׁל אֵשׁ אֵרֵד וַאֲקָרֵר מִבִּפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the replacement plan after rejecting the hail angel's offer in step 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fire angel cooling the furnace from within would be a true miracle that displays הקב״ה's power.
